section_summary: This section follows the Showa Denko scandal, the fall of the Ashida Cabinet, and the formation and prospects of Shigeru Yoshida’s government. Later records describe a Cabinet Committee on Public Safety, railway staff reductions, labor activity, and Yoshida’s views on a peace treaty. Several despatches include translated newspaper editorials and confidential committee papers.

subfiles.title: A Blessing in Disguise
subfiles.about: The editorial argues that public anger over the Showa Denko scandal could help end official corruption.
subfiles.summary: Public outrage may compel a lasting cleanup of government corruption.

subfiles.title: Various Parties’ Attitude Toward New Regime
subfiles.doc_type: translated press report; enclosure to Tokyo despatch 662
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The report surveys party responses to the Ashida Cabinet’s resignation.
subfiles.summary: Parties debate a coalition, a temporary election cabinet, and possible Yoshida or Yamazaki premierships after the Showa Denko arrests.

subfiles.title: Installation and Composition of the Yoshida Cabinet
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The airgram reports the installation, membership, and expected parliamentary difficulties of Yoshida’s Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Yoshida’s single party Cabinet took office on October 19. Its limited Diet support led observers to expect a short tenure or an election.

subfiles.title: Further Appointments to the Yoshida Cabinet
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The airgram supplements the earlier cabinet list with appointments and resignations.
subfiles.summary: It reports additional Democratic Liberal advisers, changes in foreign affairs posts, and the appointment of a liaison office director.

subfiles.title: Resignation of Minister of Finance after Scandal in Diet
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch reports Sanroku Izumiyama’s resignation after allegations of misconduct at a Diet gathering.
subfiles.summary: Izumiyama resigned his Cabinet posts and Diet seat after Yamashita Harue accused him of misconduct. The despatch recounts conflicting claims, press reaction, temporary replacements, and concern about public trust in representative government.

subfiles.title: Yoshida’s Remarks on a Possible United States Visit
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The airgram assesses press reports that Yoshida was willing to visit the United States.
subfiles.summary: Yoshida’s remark appeared incidental to a wide ranging interview, rather than a specific proposal for a visit.

subfiles.title: Japanese Cabinet Committee on Public Safety
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, Chargé d’Affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: The despatch introduces a confidential Cabinet committee and forwards its membership and working papers.
subfiles.summary: The Cabinet created a Public Safety Committee and a more active preparatory committee to review threats to public order. The Foreign Office supplied confidential papers on railway cuts, Koreans in Japan, and labor groups.

subfiles.title: Membership of Cabinet Committee and Preparatory Committee on Public Safety
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The enclosure names the members of the two public safety committees.
subfiles.summary: Lists Cabinet members and senior officials serving on both committees.

subfiles.title: Information Concerning the Personnel Reduction of Government Railway
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The paper assesses possible railway strikes following further staff reductions.
subfiles.summary: It considers strike timing, possible cooperation among unions and Korean groups, reported Communist instructions around Osaka and Suita, and railway authorities’ concerns about rehiring repatriates.

subfiles.title: National Railway Trouble and Attitude of Koreans in Japan
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The paper describes the League of Koreans in Japan’s proposed role in labor disputes.
subfiles.summary: It reports League plans to support railway workers and pursue demands concerning education, taxes, food, and livelihood. It also speculates that the League might adopt less visible tactics.

subfiles.title: Information on the Proposed Personnel Adjustment of the National Railway Corporation
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The paper reviews railway union divisions, a railway accident, and communications disruptions.
subfiles.summary: It reports a possible union split, regional unrest, the Mitaka accident, and severed communications cables.

subfiles.title: Present Strength and Policies of the Main Labor Groups on the Eve of the Summer Labor Offensive
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The survey lists union membership and compares policies for the anticipated summer labor offensive.
subfiles.summary: Tables enumerate railway, communications, government, mining, transport, shipbuilding, automobile, and other unions. They compare positions on wages, staff cuts, labor laws, political alliances, and methods of struggle.

subfiles.title: Yoshida Press Interview on Cabinet, Economy, and Peace
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The airgram reproduces Yoshida’s October 9 interview on domestic and foreign policy.
subfiles.summary: Yoshida rejected an immediate Cabinet change or further yen devaluation and discussed taxes, unemployment, China, foreign investment, and prospects for a peace treaty.

subfiles.title: Events Leading up to the Election of Mr. Yoshida Shigeru as Prime Minister and the Precarious Nature of His Cabinet
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch analyzes Yoshida’s selection and the political and economic pressures facing his Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Drawing on a conversation with Matsumoto Takizo and press editorials, it describes opposition to Yoshida, the failed Yamazaki candidacy and coalition proposal, and disagreement over when to dissolve the Diet. It also weighs Yoshida’s popularity against difficult promises on economic controls, corruption, and labor policy.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Matsumoto Takizo
subfiles.about: Matsumoto recounts efforts to prevent Yoshida’s election and to form a national coalition.
subfiles.summary: Matsumoto describes the collapse of the Ashida Cabinet, Yamazaki’s proposed candidacy, and interviews with General MacArthur by Yoshida and Miki. He discusses opposition parties’ strategy, Yoshida’s appeal, and MacArthur’s concern over scandals and labor problems.

subfiles.title: Heighth of Stupidity
subfiles.about: The editorial condemns the maneuver to nominate Yamazaki and his resulting Diet resignation.
subfiles.summary: It argues that Yoshida, as opposition leader, was the logical choice to succeed Ashida and criticizes the proposed national coalition.

subfiles.title: Mr. Yoshida as Prime Minister
subfiles.about: The editorial urges support for Yoshida’s new government while assessing its weaknesses.
subfiles.summary: It expects a short and stormy administration because of weak Diet support, party strains, and labor opposition.

subfiles.title: How Soon Until the Next Election?
subfiles.about: The editorial considers when the Yoshida government might dissolve the Diet.
subfiles.summary: It argues that campaign costs and party calculations could delay an election despite public interest in an early vote.

subfiles.title: Fulfill Public Commitments
subfiles.about: The editorial presses Yoshida to carry out promised economic and administrative changes.
subfiles.summary: It calls for selective economic decontrol, enforcement against corruption, and reductions in government staffing.

subfiles.title: Labor and the New Government
subfiles.about: The editorial examines labor opposition and proposed changes to labor law under Yoshida.
subfiles.summary: It cautions that restrictive laws could radicalize workers and urges unions to assess the Cabinet’s actual policy.

subfiles.title: Draft of Yoshida’s Foreign Affairs Policy Statement
subfiles.about: Sebald transmits confidential excerpts from Yoshida’s planned statement on peace and Japan’s security.
subfiles.summary: The draft calls for an early peace treaty with as many powers as possible and describes its expected psychological and economic benefits. It discusses debate over total or separate peace, Japan’s constitutional renunciation of war, and the unresolved question of security after occupation.

subfiles.title: Postponement of Yoshida’s Policy Statement
subfiles.about: Sebald reports a delay in the policy statement discussed in his previous telegram.
subfiles.summary: Yoshida’s policy statement was reportedly postponed, probably until January 20.
